title: Midday scratch: refactor signal mapping and micro-PR plan
content:
TL;DR:
Quick personal dump of thoughts for PR #2481 (signal-mapping + kv-cache routing tweak). Capture small, testable micro-PRs, quick safety checks, and a lightweight rollout plan. This is a scratchpad — incomplete thoughts, hypotheses, and a few manual steps.

Context (short):
- PR: optimize routing for prefix/KV cache hits when model variants are served across tiers.
- Goal: reduce unnecessary cache misses and cross-host fetches for short-prefix-heavy workloads (search reranking, short-chat).
- Observed: tail latency jumps under specific request distributions; trace shows repeated KV fetches across hosts because mapping consistency is slightly off under autoscaling.
- Customer impact: visible in a small set of customers on Dedicated; risk of higher per-token cost and SLO violations.

Quick review checklist (my brain dump):
- Safety (must check before merge):
  - [ ] Unit tests for new mapping function boundary cases (no prefixes, long prefixes, null kv-id).
  - [ ] Integration test that simulates autoscale add/remove of nodes and verifies consistent routing for same prefix across ephemeral topology changes.
  - [ ] Backwards compatibility: confirm old routing key format still resolves to same cache bucket (if reading old cache entries).
  - [ ] Telemetry: ensure new code emits metric tags: routing_strategy=stable|fallback, cache_miss_reason=map_mismatch|expired.
  - [ ] Ensure the fallback code path (if mapping fails) increments a gauge and triggers an alert on sustained rate.

- Testing/perf:
  - [ ] Add a synthetic benchmark to running e2e perf suite with a 70/30 short/long prefix mix. Look for 95p latency and p99 improvements.
  - [ ] Run a canary on a small Dedicated pool, traffic slice ~1% with high short-prefix ratio.

Refactor ideas (small and incremental):
- Idea A: Extract mapping logic to a small well-documented module (signal_map.py -> SignalMap class) with a single public method: resolve(prefix)->bucket_id. Keeps PR surface focused.
  - Rationale: isolates complexity, easier to mock in tests, can be swapped at runtime during rollout.

- Idea B: Replace inlined hashing + modulus with a two-step deterministic shard algorithm (hash -> stable-cuckoo step -> bucket). This reduces collision spikes when the node count toggles.
  - Risk: introduces a different distribution; must validate uniformity.

- Idea C: Add a short-lived sticky-cache layer per router (in-memory LRU TTL 30s) that caches resolve(prefix) results to avoid repeated recomputation for bursty workloads.
  - Note: cheap and likely big win for short-lived bursts; watch memory pressure.

Micro-PRs (split for easier review and rollback):
1) signal-map-extract: move existing logic into new SignalMap class + tests (small).
2) stable-shard: implement two-step shard algorithm behind feature flag; unit tests + distribution analysis.
3) sticky-ttl: add per-router LRU cache with opt-in config; perf test only.
4) telemetry-and-alerting: add metrics/tags and a one-off alert playbook (thresholds, pager path).
5) rollout-script: add k8s job/helm flag to enable feature flag for single pool, plus a small load-generator script in tools/ that reproduces failure mode.

Rollout plan (rough):
- Step 0: Merge micro-PR #1 (extract) to make subsequent reviews fast. Keep toggles off.
- Step 1: Deploy stable-shard behind FF to a single pool; enable telemetry. Observe for 24-48h.
- Step 2: If stable, enable sticky-ttl on same pool.
- Step 3: Canary to 5% more pools. If regressions, flip FF and rely on fallback.

Manual verification steps (local/dev):
- Start local router with test pool: `./dev/run_router --pool test-pool --feature-flag stable-shard=false`
- Run `tools/loadgen --pattern short-prefix-heavy --qps 200 --duration 10m` and capture traces to `tmp/traces/`
- Enable `stable-shard` and re-run; compare `kv_fetch_count` per-request distribution.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Q1: Are there any downstream components relying on the previous non-determinism (unlikely but check solutions-engineering tickets).
- Q2: How will the stable-shard interact with cross-region fallback routing? Might increase cross-region affinity unintentionally. Need test scenario for multi-region routing.
- Q3: Are there any models with extremely long prefix chains where the mapping resolution cost becomes non-trivial? (Profiling needed).

Potential pitfalls and guardrails:
- If the new mapping reduces collisions but increases skew, we could overload a single host. Add a host-load sanity check in the router: if load(bucket)>1.8x median, trigger fallback to generic hashing.
- Avoid changing serialization format of the routing key. If we need to, include a version header and migration path.

Cleanup & follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add a short Confluence note summarizing the algorithm, why we chose it, and expected impact (owning it from eng-serving-runtime doc space).
- Schedule a 30m sync with Solutions Eng to run a replay for top 3 affected customers (Ethan to coordinate).
- Add a small eval that measures token-cost delta for typical workloads and attach to PR.

Estimated effort (very rough):
- signal-map-extract: 0.5–1d
- stable-shard impl + tests + perf: 2–3d
- sticky-ttl + memory guard: 1d
- telemetry/alerting + playbook: 0.5d
- rollout automation + loadgen: 1d

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep PRs < 300 LOC each. Review fatigue is real.
- Talk to infra about a lightweight metric to track mapping churn (how often resolve(prefix) changes bucket over N minutes).
- If we see >0.5% requests flipping buckets during scale events -> revert to generic fallback and investigate further.

Scratchpad end. Will tidy if I convert to RFC. For now: do signal-map-extract first and loop in Maya for tests and Ethan for rollout script.
